(NYSE: PHIN), (“PHINIA”, or the “Company”), a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. THIRD QUARTER 2026 HIGHLIGHTS: (all comparisons versus the prior-year period) • Net sales increased 0.4% to $912 million; excluding the impact of foreign currency, net sales remained flat year over year. • Net earnings of $67 million, or $1.80 per diluted share; Adjusted net earnings of $68 million, or $1.83 per adjusted diluted share, an increase from $1.59 last year. • Adjusted EBITDA increased $2 million to $135 million; Adjusted EBITDA margin rate was 14.8%, an increase of 20 basis points (bps). • Stable execution on return of capital program; repurchased $65 million of common equity under existing share repurchase authorization, paid $11 million in cash dividends. “Our third quarter results were consistent with our expectations and reflect stable end market demand, continued aftermarket momentum, and strong financial discipline,” said Brady Ericson, President and Chief Executive Officer of PHINIA. “We generated another quarter of profitable growth, with Adjusted EBITDA increasing $2 million, or 20 bps, despite higher R&D spending and investments in customer relationships, demonstrating the resilience of our business and consistent execution. Based on our solid third quarter results and the continued business momentum, we are updating our fiscal 2026 financial guidance. “We made further progress on our key strategic priorities during the quarter, highlighted by strong new award activity in targeted growth markets and consistent execution on our disciplined capital allocation strategy. Our business momentum continued into the third quarter, as we delivered strong new award activity, with awards focused on emerging growth industries. Importantly, we returned $76 million of capital to shareholders during the quarter, which represents 104% of adjusted free cash flow, and we remain committed to our balanced capital allocation strategy, which is focused on investments for growth, strategic acquisitions, and capital returns. “We are focused on building a diversified growth business, driven by strong product leadership, expansion into growth markets, product innovation, and disciplined financial execution. Our strong new business momentum and consistent financial results are evidence our strategy is working. We remain committed to our strategic framework and confident in our ability to execute on our key priorities, all with a focus on delivering value for our shareholders,” concluded Ericson. CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL RESULTS PHINIA delivered third quarter net sales of $912 million, an increase of 0.4% when compared to the prior-year period. Excluding the impact of foreign currency of $4 million, net sales remained flat year over year. Results in both periods were impacted by tariff-related customer recovery mechanisms. Third quarter 2025 benefitted from net sales associated with tariff cost recoveries, while third quarter 2026 reflected 1 reductions in net sales related to tariff cost refunds to be returned to customers. Excluding the effects of this tariff-related volatility, core business sales increased $21 million year-over-year. Power Systems net sales declined 1.8% to $561 million primarily reflecting the non-recurrence of favorable customer pricing actions realized in the prior year and the timing of tariff recovery mechanisms with customers. Aftermarket Solutions net sales increased 4.2% to $351 million driven by higher sales in the Americas, partially offset by the timing of tariff recovery mechanisms with customers. The Company reported net earnings of $67 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $135 million. The year-over-year increase in Adjusted EBITDA was driven primarily by higher sales volume in the Americas and the favorable timing of tariff recovery mechanisms, partially offset by increased R&D investment and the non-recurrence of favorable customer pricing actions realized in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 20 basis points year-over-year to 14.8% , primarily reflecting the timing of tariff recovery mechanisms. BUSINESS UPDATE During the third quarter of 2026, PHINIA continued to advance its multi-year value creation strategy across its commercial, operational, and capital allocation priorities. The following highlights key progress achieved during the three months ended September 30, 2026. Commercial Update PHINIA secured several new business awards and expanded its global distribution reach, including the following: • First methanol engine program, extending PHINIA’s technology into alternative fuels and industrial off-highway applications in China. • New compressed natural gas (CNG) injector program for the Indian light passenger vehicle market, strengthening PHINIA’s position across diverse fuels, applications, and regions. • GDI pump award for a new range-extender application in North America, demonstrating the continued relevance of PHINIA technology across evolving powertrain architectures. • New customer win for the North American fuel injector remanufacturing business, expanding the diesel customer base. • Won competitive-conquest Aftermarket braking business in Spain and expanded Southeast Asian distribution, including increased penetration of steering & suspension products. • Secured new business across diesel, vehicle electronics and engine management systems (EMS) in Saudi Arabia, Portugal and Spain, expanding customer and product penetration. BALANCE SHEET AND CASH FLOW As of September 30, 2026, PHINIA had total cash and cash equivalents of $436 million and $377 million of availability under its Revolving Credit Facility, resulting in total available liquidity of $813 million . Total debt at the end of the third quarter 2026 was $1.1 billion, with net leverage of 1.3x . Net cash generated by operating activities was $87 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of $32 million, primary due to withholding tax payments related to cash repatriation and an unfavorable working capital impact, which was primarily driven by an increase in accounts receivable, reflecting the timing of customer collections and higher receivable balances at quarter-end. Adjusted free cash flow was $73 million, a decrease of $31 million compared to the third quarter of 2025. 2 FINANCIAL GUIDANCE The following forward-looking guidance reflects PHINIA’S current expectations and beliefs as of October 29, 2026, and is subject to change. About PHINIA PHINIA is a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, with a strong portfolio of trusted brands that includes DELPHI®, DELCO REMY®, and HARTRIDGE TM and stoba ® . With over 100 years of manufacturing expertise and industry relationships, PHINIA has approximately 13,500 talented employees and over 40 locations in 21 countries and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA. Our systems and solutions are designed to keep combustion engines operating at peak performance across a variety of applications: medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified class 4-8, 14,001 pounds or heavier), light commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified as class 1-3, 14,000 pounds or lighter), light passenger vehicle (on-road vehicles used primarily for carrying passengers), and off-highway, industrial, and other (including construction and agricultural machinery, vocational vehicles, marine, industrial applications, power generation, and aerospace and defense). PHINIA’s service solutions include vehicle repair and replacement parts, offering both new and remanufactured products through the original equipment manufacturer dealer network and the independent aftermarket channel. By delivering high-performance solutions today and investing in advanced technologies to unlock the potential of alternative fuels in contributing to lower carbon mobility, PHINIA is shaping a more efficient and sustainable future. © 2026 PHINIA Inc. Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin The Company defines adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) as net earnings less interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, adjusted to exclude the impact of restructuring expense, separation-related costs, merger and acquisition costs, other postretirement income and expense, equity in affiliates' earnings, net of tax, impairment charges, other net expenses, and other gains and losses not reflective of our ongoing operations. Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as adjusted EBITDA divided by net sales. Management utilizes adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin in its financial decision-making process and to evaluate performance of the Company's consolidated results. Management also believes adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA margin are useful to investors in assessing the Company’s ongoing consolidated financial performance, as they provide improved comparability between periods through the exclusion of certain items that management believes are not indicative of the Company’s core operating performance. Adjusted Net Earnings and Adjusted Net Earnings Per Diluted Share The Company defines adjusted net earnings and adjusted net earnings per diluted share as net earnings and net earnings per share, each adjusted to exclude: (i) the tax-effected impact of restructuring expense, separation-related costs, merger and acquisition costs, impairment charges and other gains, losses and tax effects and adjustments not reflective of the Company’s ongoing operations; and (ii) acquisition-related intangibles amortization expense because it pertains to non-cash expenses that the Company does not use to evaluate core operating performance. Management believes that adjusted net earnings and adjusted net earnings per diluted share are useful to investors in assessing the Company’s ongoing financial performance, as they provide improved comparability between periods through the exclusion of certain items that management believes are not indicative of the Company’s core operating performance. 9 Adjusted Free Cash Flow The Company defines adjusted free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities after adding back adjustments related to the ongoing effects of separation-related transactions, less capital expenditures, including tooling outlays. Management believes that adjusted free cash flow is useful to investors in assessing the Company's ability to service and repay its debt and return capital to shareholders. Further, management uses this non-GAAP measure for planning and forecasting purposes. Net Leverage The Company defines net leverage as net debt divided by trailing twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA. Management believes this measure is useful to investors in assessing the Company’s leverage profile and ability to service its debt obligations.
